target_customer: HR teams and employers hiring international candidates
problem: Screening candidates for visa eligibility and compliance is manual and creates legal risk when hiring across borders.
business_model: B2B SaaS plug-in for HR systems; pricing not public
product_category: AI immigration screening and compliance for HR

technical_complexity.rationale: Document parsing and visa pathway classification with LLMs is standard, but legal accuracy and HR system integrations add difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Immigration law firms, platforms and global mobility vendors were also adding AI, and integrations are the main stickiness.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Vialto launched an AI immigration assessment tool in 2026; no acquisition of Mayflower found.

market_need_then: Employers face legal exposure when hiring global candidates and the company cites manual screening; SHRM coverage describes workplace immigration technology as booming.

branding.domain_note: Uses mayflowervisa.com, a suffix domain; the plain name evokes the Pilgrim ship, which fits immigration, but no source states this was the intent.

identity.logo: simple black wordmark in capital letters

brand_strength.rationale: A memorable real word with an immigration connotation, but no press, community or sourced brand assets.

outcome_analysis: Mayflower is a two-person Fall 2025 YC company building an HR plug-in for immigration screening. No verified funding, customers or outcome events are public, and larger mobility and legal vendors are adding similar AI tools. There is not enough evidence to judge whether it will stall or succeed.
notes: Competitor list left empty: the only dated entrants found (Vialto, August 2026; eazyPetition, Immplify) are not dated near the batch. VCBacked reports $500K pre-seed in December 2025 and PitchBook a January 2025 date for the same $500K; both aggregators, unverified, likely the YC deal, so no round recorded.
